submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires on the closed-class 'glue' tokens that open or continue a slot for more material: the determiners, quantifiers and possessives that introduce a new or additional referent (a, some, several, few, many, each, other, another, own, my, our, your) and the connectives and separators that open a further clause, member or line (':', ';', ' and', ' or', ' including', '//' at a comment-line start); those reach 1.0-2.6 of the 2.74 maximum while content words, rare words, plain commas and non-Latin-script tokens sit at 0-0.3. For a fixed word it peaks at a complement or enumeration boundary rather than inside a given phrase (a after has/have/and 1.25-1.38 vs after as/in 0.27-0.50; the after than/be/have 0.91-1.16 vs after for/in/over 0.08-0.27), a preference that still rides on top of an unexplained positive offset across German text.

rival_explanations: Language detector: the pole is really a German/non-English text detector (German documents average 0.89 against 0.20 for English, 58% of their tokens above the active threshold), so the English determiner and colon peaks are incidental and any German text, content words included, should be predicted active.

Line/format-break predictor: the pole marks where a line or formatted block ends and the model should emit a newline or period, which is why list colons before '\n', '//' at a comment-line start, and 'Copyright ... All rights reserved.' dominate the peaks, and plain running prose without such structure should be predicted inactive.

Token-frequency neuron: it merely tracks a handful of very frequent closed-class types (a, the, and, other, some) and no context beyond the current token matters, so its activation should be constant for a given token and the same word should fire equally in every frame.

Эрик Уолдер (; ) — американский легкоатлет, специалист по прыжкам в длину и тройным прыжкам. Выступал за сборную США по лёгкой атлетике в 1990-х годах, обладатель серебряной медали чемпионата мира, двукратный бронзовый призёр чемпионатов мира в помещении, двукратный серебряный призёр Игр доброй воли. Дважды показывал лучшие результаты мирового сезона в прыжках в длину (1994, 1996).

Биография 
Эрик Уолдер родился 5 ноября 1971 года в городе Мобил, штат Алабама.

Занимался лёгкой атлетикой во время учёбы в Университете Арканзаса, в составе университетской команды Arkansas Razorbacks успешно выступал на различных студенческих соревнованиях, в том числе 10 раз выигрывал чемпионаты Национальной ассоциации студенческого спорта в прыжках в длину и тройных прыжках — как на открытом стадионе, так и в помещении.

Впервые заявил о себе на международном уровне в сезоне 1990 года, когда вошёл в состав американской сборной и выступил на юниорском мировом первенстве в Пловдиве, где в зачёте тройного прыжка занял итоговое 15-е место.

В 1993 году стал четвёртым в прыжках в длину на чемпионате мира в Штутгарте.

В 1994 году на соревнованиях в Эль-Пасо установил свой личный рекорд в прыжках в длину и показал лучший результат мирового сезона — 8,74 метра. В той же дисциплине завоевал серебряную награду на Играх доброй воли в Санкт-Петербурге, уступив только своему титулованному соотечественнику Майку Пауэллу.

В 1995 году выиграл бронзовую медаль на чемпионате мира в помещении в Барселоне.

В мае 1996 года на соревнованиях в Спрингфилде превзошёл всех соперников, показав при этом лучший результат мирового сезона — 8,58 метра.

In effetti è vero, c’è un po’ di confusione sulle maschere viso, soprattutto perché fino a qualche anno fa erano poche quelle in commercio, mentre negli ultimi anni abbiamo assistito ad un boom incredibile! Partiamo subito con la scelta della maschera che, hai detto bene, si fa in base al proprio tipo di pelle.
Intanto è bene capire che la maschera viso è un trattamento intensivo extra alla propria skincare routine, che deve essere sempre curata e giusta per le nostre abitudini. Proprio per questo la maschera si sceglie non solo in base alla pelle, ma anche alle necessità del periodo o del momento in cui la si utilizza. Una pelle grassa, ad esempio, tenderà a scegliere maschere purificanti, opacizzanti e riequilibranti, ma ciò non vieta che non possa fare una maschera lenitiva, ad esempio se sente la pelle tirare o idratante, se la pelle è un po’ più secca a causa di un periodo stressante, di utilizzo di prodotti errati o troppo aggressivi. Al tempo stesso, una pelle secca tenderà ad utilizzare prevalentemente maschere nutrienti ed idratanti, più ricche, ma ciò non toglie che in caso di uno sfogo di imperfezioni o per contrastare i punti neri, non possa utilizzarne una purificante o esfoliante.
Tutto sta nello scegliere una maschera adatta alla pelle ed alle esigenze o, ancora meglio, usarle in sinergia. Dopo aver effettuato una maschera purificante, che va ad agire sulle imperfezioni, si può applicarne una idratante, prestando attenzione che non sia comedogena e non contenga oli o sostanze troppo pesanti, per non vanificare l’effetto della prima utilizzata. O, ancora si possono combinare varie maschere in varie parti del viso, nel caso di una pelle mista, come ad esempio una purificante o all’argilla sulla zona T che tende a lucidarsi e una idratante sulle guance e collo, per effettuare il cosiddetto multimasking.
Non c’è una regola sulla frequenza con cui applicare le maschere viso, l’importante è ascoltare la propria pelle. C’è chi le fa tutti i giorni o a giorni alterni, chi preferisce distanziare le applicazioni e dedicarcisi solo una volta a settimana. Questo dipende da come la propria pelle reagisce, alcune hanno bisogno di tanti prodotti e di varietà, altre invece prediligono una skincare minima, senza stratificare troppi prodotti e senza sovraccaricare la pelle. Infatti, in alcuni casi “il troppo stroppia” e, invece di ottenere risultati benefici dall’applicazione di tante maschere, potrebbe capitare di ritrovarsi con la comparsa di imperfezioni, brufoletti sottopelle o lucidità ed untuosità nella zona T.
Un capitolo va poi dedicato alle varie tipologie di maschere viso, che sono davvero tantissime. What Are Company Values? (With Definition And Examples)
Updated 14 October 2022
The Indeed Editorial Team comprises a diverse and talented team of writers, researchers and subject matter experts equipped with Indeed's data and insights to deliver useful tips to help guide your career journey.
Many companies define a set of values and share these standards with their employees and consumers. These values can help influence business decisions and help create a collaborative and supportive professional environment. Understanding a company culture and what principles an organisation values can help professionals determine whether it is the right workplace for them, and allow customers to evaluate whether they want to support a brand.
In this article, we define what company values are, describe why they are important, explore the benefits of identifying them and provide examples of values companies use.
What Are Company Values?
Company values are the standards and guidelines that drive an organisation's business operations. These values can influence how internal teams function, the products and services a company offers and the type of marketing materials and public messaging a brand shares. They can define behavioural norms and help staff members understand management's expectations and priorities.
Here is a list of common examples of principles a company may value:
Communicate often and well
Listen to ideas and opinions
Have high standards
Put the customer first
Create an inclusive environment
Be a leader
Treat the customer right
Do not be afraid to fail
Practice social responsibility
Related: Core Values: Overview And Examples
Why Are These Values Important?
These values are important because they allow a company to define what it prioritises, and inform internal employees and customers of these principles. This can help an organisation attract employees whose beliefs align with the brand, which can help professionals feel satisfied and committed to the company and its success. It can also help a company's marketing and advertising teams develop materials that target members of a particular audience and grow the company's client base overall.
These values can help a company's employees make decisions that benefit the organisation and allow it to succeed. They can also attract investors, customers and new employees who share the same belief system. Core values create a company's culture and inspire its business strategy, and this equates to a company's success since everyone is working towards the same goals.
What Are The Benefits Of Having Company Values?
Having strong corporate values can benefit a business in a variety of ways, including:
Creating a stronger brand identity: When core values accurately portray the purpose of a company it can help create and promote the company's brand. People may associate the company and its products with the core values it projects, which can grow a business's client base and foster customer loyalty.

readings.explanation: This pole fires on the closed-class 'glue' tokens that open or continue a slot for more material: the determiners, quantifiers and possessives that introduce a new or additional referent (a, some, several, few, many, each, other, another, own, my, our, your) and the connectives and separators that open a further clause, member or line (':', ';', ' and', ' or', ' including', '//' at a comment-line start); those reach 1.0-2.6 of the 2.74 maximum while content words, rare words, plain commas and non-Latin-script tokens sit at 0-0.3. For a fixed word it peaks at a complement or enumeration boundary rather than inside a given phrase (a after has/have/and 1.25-1.38 vs after as/in 0.27-0.50; the after than/be/have 0.91-1.16 vs after for/in/over 0.08-0.27), a preference that still rides on top of an unexplained positive offset across German text.

Language detector: the pole is really a German/non-English text detector (German documents average 0.89 against 0.20 for English, 58% of their tokens above the active threshold), so the English determiner and colon peaks are incidental and any German text, content words included, should be predicted active.

Line/format-break predictor: the pole marks where a line or formatted block ends and the model should emit a newline or period, which is why list colons before '\n', '//' at a comment-line start, and 'Copyright ... All rights reserved.' dominate the peaks, and plain running prose without such structure should be predicted inactive.

Token-frequency neuron: it merely tracks a handful of very frequent closed-class types (a, the, and, other, some) and no context beyond the current token matters, so its activation should be constant for a given token and the same word should fire equally in every frame.

verdict.notes: positive_holdout: 9/10 passed; hard_negative: 4/20 passed; counterfactual: 6/6 passed; lookahead_consistency: 1/1 passed. Failed gates: specificity, beats_confound_baseline.
